From the extension code you’re using (the Click2Crawl schema format), URLs are only extracted if: 1. `type === 'attribute'`, **and** 2. An `attribute` name is provided. See `testSchema()`: ```js this.schema.fields.forEach(field => { try { const element = container.querySelector(field.selector); if (element) { if (field.type === 'text') { item[field.name] = element.textContent.trim(); } else if (field.type === 'attribute' && field.attribute) { item[field.name] = element.getAttribute(field.attribute); } } else { item[field.name] = null; } } catch (e) { item[field.name] = null; } }); ``` So: - There is **no special `url` type** handled anywhere, only `text` and `attribute`. - To get the `href`, you must use `type: "attribute"` and `attribute: "href"`. Also, base and field selectors are expected to be **CSS selectors**, not XPath. The schema uses `document.querySelectorAll(this.schema.baseSelector)` and `container.querySelector(field.selector)`, which only support CSS, not XPath. ### Fixing your schema Assuming your table row looks like: ```html Cell 1 Cell 2 Cell 3 View Download ``` Define your schema like this: ```python pubs_schema = { "name": "news", "baseSelector": "tr", "fields": [ { "name": "Reference", "selector": "td:nth-child(1)", "type": "text", }, { "name": "Description", "selector": "td:nth-child(2)", "type": "text", }, { "name": "Date", "selector": "td:nth-child(3)", "type": "text", }, { "name": "View", "selector": "td:nth-child(4) > a", "type": "attribute", "attribute": "href", }, { "name": "Download", "selector": "td:nth-child(5) > a", "type": "attribute", "attribute": "href", }, ], } ``` Key changes: - `View` selector: switched from invalid XPath (`"//tr/td[4]/a[/@href"`) to a **CSS selector**: `"td:nth-child(4) > a"`. - `Download` selector: simplified to `"td:nth-child(5) > a"` (the `a:nth-child(1)` part is unnecessary unless you really have multiple links). - For both link fields: - `type` is now `"attribute"`. - `attribute` is set to `"href"`.
